newsitem.title: FRANCE: French planters now see steady 97/98 beet area.
newsitem.headline: French planters now see steady 97/98 beet area.

text.p: French planters now predict the area sown to sugar beets for the 1997/98 season may remain broadly similar to the 422,000 hectares sown in 1996/97.
In February planters had predicted sowings might increase by one to two percent.
But the results of an extensive planters survey conducted by the French sugar beet planters federation (CGB) now suggest the area will remain unchanged.
"This is rather surprising as we first expected a slight increase. At this stage we do not expect a change in area," a CGB analyst told Reuters on Friday.
Farmers had no incentive to plant more beets this year in view of lower world prices and a higher sugar carryover, the analyst said.
The latest statistics from the national sugar intervention board FIRS showed France produced 4.23 million tonnes of beet sugar in 1996/97.
The 1997/98 sugar campaign got under way last week in France, with planters hopeful that sowings might be completed by the end of the month.
But sowings were behind last year's level as scattered rain earlier this week prevented farmers from getting into the fields.
"At this stage we are ahead of the last five-year average though we are slightly behind last year," the analyst said.
Planters were, however, hoping to make good progress in the coming days as weather services had forecast dry weather conditions.
"We are hoping to complete sowings by the end of next week, if favourable weather holds," he added.
As of March 20, an average seven percent of the area had been sown to sugar beets against 17 percent at the same stage last year.
But there were great variations depending on regions, he said.
Some 50 percent of the area had been sown in the Loiret region in central France and in Burgundy in the east.
But the area sown to sugar beets stood at only two percent in the main production area of Picardie in northern France, at two percent in the Oise region and at 4-5 percent in Normandy.
